body:
## What does freeze-dried instant coffee mean for an Indian kitchen?

Freeze-drying skips the liquid stage entirely. Frozen coffee concentrate goes straight from solid to vapor under vacuum, so the aromatic oils that usually disappear in high-heat spray drying stay locked inside the granule. The result is a lighter, porous crystal that rehydrates instantly and tastes much closer to a freshly pulled shot. In an Indian kitchen where the geyser hisses and mornings move fast, that speed matters — you get cafe-quality depth without the wait. A practical tip: use water just off the boil, around 92–94°C, and stir gently; the granules bloom in seconds and you avoid the scorched note that rolling-boil water can leave. Purity Beans applies this method to its Purica and Purista jars, while the Bold jar uses agglomeration for a denser granule that holds up in milk-heavy cups. Ultra Blend sits at 70% coffee and 30% chicory for drinkers who want a familiar, everyday balance, and Prima is a pure Arabica agglomerate that is not freeze-dried. Pick the process that matches how you actually brew.

### A plain definition

Whatever brought you here, the label settles it. The other single jars on this page are 0% chicory.

## How do you read the chicory line on the jar?

Turn the jar around and find the ingredient list. That is the only line that matters. If it says chicory, the blend contains chicory — no marketing phrase on the front can change that. At Purity Beans, Bold, Purista, and Purica all show coffee as the single ingredient because they are pure coffee with zero chicory. Purista and Purica are freeze-dried granules; Bold is agglomerated pure coffee. A quick rule of thumb: the higher chicory sits on the list, the more of it you are drinking. Some brands tuck it near the bottom and hope you won't check. Prima is pure Arabica but it is agglomerated, not freeze-dried, so the process line will read differently. Next time you pick up a jar, ignore the flavor adjectives and read the ingredients. That five-second habit tells you more than any advertisement ever will.

## Which jar suits the way you drink coffee?

Choosing a jar comes down to how you actually drink your coffee. If you reach for a mug of black coffee first thing in the morning and want that deep, honest kick, Bold is the one — it's agglomerated, strong, and priced at ₹369 for 100g. For afternoons when you want something smooth with natural crema, Purista brings freeze-dried Robusta at ₹509 for 100g. And if your ideal cup leans aromatic with caramel and chocolate notes, Purica delivers freeze-dried Arabica at ₹559 for 100g. Not sure where you land? The Variety Box (₹877 for four 50g jars) lets you taste all four side by side. Purity Beans keeps it simple: match the jar to the ritual, and you will never waste money on coffee that does not fit your morning.

## What does each jar cost in rupees?

If you are budgeting for a shelf of Purity Beans jars, here is how the prices break down today. The 50g Bold Pure Coffee starts at ₹239 and the 100g at ₹369 — both are agglomerated pure coffee with zero chicory. Purista Gourmet Robusta Granules, which are freeze-dried, come in at ₹319 for 50g and ₹509 for 100g. Purica Gourmet Arabica Granules, also freeze-dried, are ₹329 for 50g and ₹559 for 100g. If you want to taste everything without committing to full sizes, the Variety Box gives you four 50g jars — Bold, Purista, Purica, and Ultra Blend — for ₹877, which saves ₹219 versus buying them separately. For a pure-coffee deep dive, the Gourmet Duo Mini pairs 50g Purista with 50g Purica at ₹570, and the full-size Gourmet Duo doubles that to two 100g jars for ₹908. Prima Premium Arabica exists at ₹269 (50g) and ₹449 (100g) but is not freeze-dried and is currently not featured. A practical tip: orders above ₹399 ship free, so any 100g jar or any bundle clears that threshold automatically.

## How do people brew instant coffee in Indian cities?

In most Indian city kitchens, the ritual is simple: water hits a rolling boil, a spoonful of granules goes into the mug, then milk and sugar follow. Some people swear by dissolving the coffee in a tiny splash of hot water first — a quick stir until it turns glossy — before topping up with steaming milk. That extra ten seconds stops the granules from clumping at the bottom. Others skip the fuss entirely and dump everything into the saucepan, letting it bubble once before pouring. Office pantries see the electric kettle method: hot water straight into the cup, a dash of cold milk to temper it, done in thirty seconds. On slower Sunday mornings, you'll find the whisk come out — vigorous back-and-forth until a thin caramel foam crowns the surface, the closest thing to cafe texture without a machine. Purity Beans drinkers often mention that the Purica and Purista jars, being freeze-dried, dissolve instantly even in cooler milk, which matters when you're rushing. The 50g Purica at ₹329 and 50g Purista at ₹319 sit beside the 50g Bold at ₹239 and the 50g Ultra Blend at ₹209 — four jars, four ways to start the day.

## How do you choose a jar without a slogan?

Walking down the coffee aisle can feel a bit overwhelming with all the loud claims staring back from every shelf. When you want a proper cup at home, reading the fine print on the back of the jar matters more than whatever catchy slogan is printed on the front. Take a quiet minute to check what is actually inside your pantry staples. If you prefer a straightforward start to your morning, the 50g Bold pure coffee jar is available at ₹239 without any guesswork. You do not need a fancy marketing pitch to figure out your morning brew; you just need to know what you are pouring into your mug. Finding the right fit is simply about matching your personal taste to honest ingredients, letting the flavor speak entirely for itself.
